title: How to choose analytics for a SaaS startup
description: A practical way for a SaaS startup to choose analytics: marketing site, product app, and revenue — without installing three tools on day one.

sections.title: Three questions, not one tool
sections.content:
A SaaS startup usually has three different questions:

1. **Marketing** — which page or channel brought the visit?
2. **Product** — did the new account do the thing that predicts they stay?
3. **Revenue** — which channel produced paid customers?

One tool can cover more than one question. Most early teams still overload a single install and then trust none of the charts.

sections.title: Start with the marketing site
sections.content:
If the site is a homepage, docs, and a signup page, a pageview tool is enough. **Plausible** or **Fathom** answer referrers, campaigns, and a signup goal without a heavy script.

Add **GA4** only if Google Ads or Search attribution is a weekly decision. Read [PostHog vs Plausible](/compare/posthog-vs-plausible/) before you put a product SDK on the marketing homepage — our recorded PostHog script is in a much heavier band than Plausible.

sections.title: Add product analytics when accounts exist
sections.content:
Once people sign in, you need a few named events: signup completed, project created, invite sent, upgrade clicked. **PostHog** is built for that, including funnels and flags. **GA4** can do events too, with more reporting overhead.

Keep the event list under ten until a chart changes a decision. The vocabulary is in [What are analytics events?](/learn/what-are-analytics-events/) and [Pageviews vs events](/learn/pageviews-vs-events/).

sections.title: Connect revenue when Stripe is the scoreboard
sections.content:
If the question is "which blog post or ad led to a paid customer," look at **DataFast**'s payment attribution or a deliberate ecommerce setup in GA4. DataFast is not a replacement for in-app funnels. Compare [Plausible vs DataFast](/compare/plausible-vs-datafast/) and [DataFast vs PostHog](/compare/datafast-vs-posthog/).

Price the shortlist at your traffic in the [pricing calculator](/calculators/pricing/) before you add a second subscription.

sections.title: A default stack
sections.content:
Marketing site: Plausible or Fathom. Product app: PostHog, once you have logged-in users. Revenue: DataFast or GA4 ecommerce, when payments are the metric that matters.

Skip the third tool until the first two leave a question you cannot answer. Heatmaps and recordings (Hotjar, or PostHog replay) come after a specific page is failing, not on day one.
